title: Helical ruler: closure density and a single-carrier branch
summary: A circular helix provides an exact per-winding ruler: axial advance per closure p, path length per closure sqrt((2πR)^2+p^2), closure density 1/p, and a scale-free shape ratio χ=p/(2πR). Current sandbox work generalizes this to nonuniform/nested helices and separates winding closure from true closed-path holonomy. A further speculative branch asks whether one global toroidal/recurrent carrier with different local deformation or jamming states could yield multiple particle-like readouts.
public_copy: A new Hagalaz-side diagnostic treats a helix as a ruler. One winding carries an axial advance, a path length, and a dimensionless pitch-to-circumference ratio. Repeating many windings lets the solver ask whether those quantities stabilize without invoking literal infinity. The same machinery can be moved onto closed toroidal windings, where topology, metric geodesicity, local deformation, and frame holonomy can be tested separately rather than conflated.
relationships: closure density -> Hagalaz integration coordinate candidate
winding closure != metric geodesic != true holonomy
